rules.subject-alarm: Alarmist wording at the start of a subject can resemble phishing or mass email.
rules.pressure: Pressure to act quickly is typical of bulk marketing messages.
rules.click-here: Generic “click here” wording resembles spam. Explain what the link is for.
rules.urgency: Urgent wording is uncommon in personalized messages.
rules.free-claim: Overemphasizing that something is free can trigger filters.
rules.free-offer: Offers of free goods or services often appear in spam.
rules.money: Promises of fast income or unusually high earnings are risky.
rules.dollars: Strong emphasis on money amounts resembles advertising.
rules.price-bait: Promotional pricing language can trigger spam filters.
rules.guarantee: Absolute guarantees are often associated with spam.
rules.no-catch: Unrequested assurances can read like a sales script.
rules.hype: Exaggerated language is less effective than a concrete explanation.
rules.prize: Winner and prize claims resemble scam messages.
rules.false-familiarity: A generic greeting suggests the message was not personalized.
rules.restricted: Terms associated with high-risk categories often trigger filters.
rules.shortener: Shortened links conceal the destination. Prefer your own domain.
rules.shouting: An all-caps word can feel like shouting.
rules.repeated-punctuation: Repeated punctuation is a common spam pattern.
rules.exclamation: Excessive exclamation marks may resemble advertising.
rules.many-links: Too many links in one message can look suspicious.

WelcomePage.heroEyebrow: Sales outreach on your own server
WelcomePage.heroTitle: LinkedIn and email, in one sequence.
WelcomePage.heroLede: Linki sends LinkedIn steps and emails side by side, hands a contact from one channel to the other, and brings every reply into a single inbox.
WelcomePage.heroAlt: The sequence builder: a LinkedIn track and an email track side by side, with conditions between the steps, and one email step open showing its four versions and its wording.
WelcomePage.selfTitle: One container, and your data stays where you put it.
WelcomePage.selfBody: Linki is software you run yourself, with no database server or queue to set up beside it.
WelcomePage.closingBody: Sign in to this Linki. If a teammate invited you, the link in their email takes you straight into their workspace.
WelcomePage.closingSignedIn: You are signed in. Your workspace is one click away.
WelcomePage.metaTitle: Linki: LinkedIn and email outreach in one sequence
WelcomePage.metaDescription: Linki runs LinkedIn steps and emails in one sequence, keeps every account and mailbox inside its limits, and brings each reply into one inbox. It runs on your own server.
WelcomePage.metaAlt: A campaign's figures in Linki: reply rate, open rate and daily activity.
WelcomePage.selfFactDetail0: The app, the API, the MCP server and the background work that sends and reads all run as a single container.
WelcomePage.selfFactDetail1: Everything is kept in a SQLite database on your own disk, so a backup is a copy of it.
WelcomePage.selfFactDetail2: Mailbox passwords, LinkedIn sessions and the keys for connected services are encrypted where they are stored. Of an API key, only a hash is kept.
WelcomePage.sec_sequences_title: Two tracks, and a path for each contact.
WelcomePage.sec_sequences_body: A campaign has a LinkedIn track and an email track that run side by side. Conditions between the steps decide what happens next, and each branch shows how many contacts took it.
WelcomePage.sec_sequences_point0: Profile visits, connection requests, LinkedIn messages and emails, with waits in hours or days.
WelcomePage.sec_sequences_point1: Conditions on an accepted connection, a reply, a verified email address, or what is known about the contact, such as an intent score.
WelcomePage.sec_sequences_point2: You choose each outcome: continue, jump ahead, end the track, leave the sequence, or hand over to the email track.
WelcomePage.sec_sequences_point3: Up to four versions of an email, split by the weights you set.
WelcomePage.sec_sequences_alt0: The LinkedIn track of a campaign: a profile visit, a connection request, a condition that hands contacts who do not accept over to the email track, a message, and a follow-up.
WelcomePage.sec_sequences_alt1: The email track of the same campaign: three emails, the first in four versions, with a condition on a verified email address and another on intent score.
WelcomePage.sec_linkedin_title: Several accounts, each inside its own limits.
WelcomePage.sec_linkedin_body: A campaign can send from a pool of LinkedIn accounts, in turn or by how much room each has left. Every account keeps its own limits, working hours and time zone, and a contact stays with the account that first reached them.
WelcomePage.sec_linkedin_point0: Daily limits for invitations, messages, profile visits and withdrawals, and a weekly invitation limit counted over a rolling seven days.
WelcomePage.sec_linkedin_point1: A warm-up that raises a new account's invitations day by day.
WelcomePage.sec_linkedin_point2: When LinkedIn ends a session or refuses an invitation, that account waits. The other accounts and the email steps carry on.
WelcomePage.sec_linkedin_point3: Sign in on the server with LinkedIn's verification code or app approval, or paste a session cookie.
WelcomePage.sec_linkedin_alt0: Three LinkedIn accounts, each with today's use against its limits for connections, messages, profile visits and withdrawals. One is on hold at its weekly invitation limit and one is on day 6 of a 21-day warm-up.
WelcomePage.sec_mailboxes_title: Mailboxes that protect their own reputation.
WelcomePage.sec_mailboxes_body: Connect Gmail with an app password, or any mailbox over SMTP and IMAP. A new mailbox starts on a low daily limit that rises each day, with warm-up running beside it.
WelcomePage.sec_mailboxes_point0: A guard pauses a mailbox when its bounce or complaint rate over 30 days crosses the threshold you set.
WelcomePage.sec_mailboxes_point1: SPF, DKIM, DMARC and MX records are checked every day, and a change to one is written to the log.
WelcomePage.sec_mailboxes_point2: Inbox placement tests show where a test email landed.
WelcomePage.sec_mailboxes_point3: One do-not-contact list for email addresses, domains, LinkedIn profiles and phone numbers, checked before every step on both channels.
WelcomePage.sec_mailboxes_alt0: Four mailboxes on one sending domain with their daily limits, warm-up state, reputation and bounce rate. One has been paused automatically after its bounce rate rose.
WelcomePage.sec_mailboxes_alt1: A sending domain scored 82 out of 100, with SPF, DKIM and MX passing and DMARC marked weak.
WelcomePage.sec_inbox_title: Every reply in one place, already read.
WelcomePage.sec_inbox_body: Email replies and LinkedIn replies arrive in the same inbox, one thread per contact. With an AI model connected, each reply is classified and summed up, and the contact's campaign is stopped or put back to match.
WelcomePage.sec_inbox_point0: Five readings of a reply: positive, needs review, out of office, negative, unsubscribe. Each comes with a confidence figure.
WelcomePage.sec_inbox_point1: Answer by email or on LinkedIn from the same box.
WelcomePage.sec_inbox_point2: Assign, snooze, tag and close. A lock shows when a teammate is already replying.
WelcomePage.sec_inbox_point3: Saved replies, and a time by which each waiting conversation is due an answer.
WelcomePage.sec_inbox_alt0: A conversation holding an email, a LinkedIn message and the contact's reply. The reply is classified as out of office with 77% confidence, and the next campaign step has been put back.
WelcomePage.sec_ai_title: AI writing on your own key, with a ceiling.
WelcomePage.sec_ai_body: Linki writes through OpenRouter with a key you supply, in a style you describe once for the workspace. Each step can have its own model, instruction, length and language.
WelcomePage.sec_ai_point0: A default model, and a fallback that takes over when the first does not answer.
WelcomePage.sec_ai_point1: A monthly budget. When it is reached, steps written by AI wait and everything else keeps sending.
WelcomePage.sec_ai_point2: Spend shown by kind of step and by model.
WelcomePage.sec_ai_point3: Try the wording on one of your contacts before anything goes out.
WelcomePage.sec_ai_alt0: The workspace's writing style: a tone, a written instruction, and example emails and LinkedIn messages for the AI to follow.
WelcomePage.sec_ai_alt1: This month's AI spend, day by day, against a monthly budget of 100 dollars.
WelcomePage.sec_audience_body: Bring people in from a Sales Navigator list or a CSV file, add what Apollo knows about them, and verify email addresses before anything is sent.
WelcomePage.sec_audience_point0: One timeline per contact: every send, open, reply and list change, across both channels.
WelcomePage.sec_audience_point1: Custom fields, tags and saved views.
WelcomePage.sec_audience_point2: Each company is kept once and linked from its contacts.
WelcomePage.sec_audience_alt0: One contact's timeline: emails sent and opened, an enrichment from Apollo, and a reply on LinkedIn.
WelcomePage.sec_reporting_title: Figures you can act on, and pass along.
WelcomePage.sec_reporting_body: A campaign shows acceptance, replies, opens, clicks and completion against the period before, a funnel from enrolled to meeting booked, and how each version of an email is doing.
WelcomePage.sec_reporting_point0: A leading version is called only when its lead is unlikely to be chance: at least 30 sends each, judged on replies before opens.
WelcomePage.sec_reporting_point1: Opens made by security scanners and mail privacy features are counted apart from people's.
WelcomePage.sec_reporting_point2: A read-only report link for someone with no account, which you can switch off at any time.
WelcomePage.sec_reporting_point3: Contacts, replies, prospects and campaign figures download as CSV.
WelcomePage.sec_reporting_alt0: Four versions of one email with the number sent, open rate and reply rate for each. It is too early to call a winner: each version needs 30 sends.
WelcomePage.sec_reporting_alt1: A campaign's funnel from 22 contacts enrolled, through contacted, accepted or opened and replied, to 2 meetings booked.
WelcomePage.sec_team_title: Five roles, and a record of every change.
WelcomePage.sec_team_body: Owner, admin, manager, member and viewer. The same roles hold in the app, the API and the MCP server.
WelcomePage.sec_team_point0: Invite a teammate by email with a link that works once and expires after seven days.
WelcomePage.sec_team_point1: An audit log of changes made on the web, through the API and through MCP, kept for 12 months.
WelcomePage.sec_team_point2: Separate workspaces, each with its own contacts, mailboxes and accounts.
WelcomePage.sec_team_alt0: The audit log: who paused a campaign, changed a role or connected an account, when, from which address, and whether through the web, the API or MCP.
WelcomePage.sec_developers_title: An API, webhooks and an MCP server.
WelcomePage.sec_developers_body: Read contacts, campaigns and their progress over a versioned API, add contacts and signals from your own systems, receive signed webhooks, or let an AI client work in Linki through its MCP server.
WelcomePage.sec_developers_point0: API keys with scopes, an expiry date and their own rate limit. Only a hash of a key is stored.
WelcomePage.sec_developers_point1: Webhooks signed with HMAC-SHA256 and tried up to eight times before they are set aside for you to look at.
WelcomePage.sec_developers_point2: An MCP client signs in through the browser and then acts with your role in the workspace you chose.
WelcomePage.sec_developers_alt0: Four webhook endpoints with the events each receives, its success rate, last delivery and status.
WelcomePage.sec_developers_alt1: The MCP server card: 79 tools, the command that adds Linki to a client, and the groups the tools fall into.

GuidedTours.welcome_0_body: Linki runs outreach on LinkedIn and email from one place. Here is where everything lives. It takes under a minute, and you can leave at any point.
GuidedTours.welcome_1_body: Everything you see belongs to one workspace. If you are a member of several, switch between them here.
GuidedTours.welcome_2_body: A campaign is a sequence of LinkedIn and email steps, run over a list of contacts. This walks you through building one.
GuidedTours.welcome_3_body: Find a contact, a company, a campaign or a list, or jump to any page. Press ⌘K (Ctrl K on Windows) from anywhere.
GuidedTours.welcome_4_body: The dashboard, the inbox where every reply lands, and your tasks.
GuidedTours.welcome_5_body: Campaigns, the message templates they draw on, and signals worth acting on.
GuidedTours.welcome_6_body: The people and companies you contact, and the lists you gather them into.
GuidedTours.welcome_7_body: The LinkedIn accounts and mailboxes campaigns send from, with their limits, and how well your email is being delivered.
GuidedTours.welcome_8_body: AI writing and its budget, integrations, your team and their roles, and the API.
GuidedTours.welcome_9_body: Sending and reading replies happen in the background, at a human pace. This says whether that work is going on.
GuidedTours.welcome_10_body: Each page has a short tour of its own. Start it, or this one, again from this menu whenever you like.
GuidedTours.dashboard_0_body: The last 7, 30 or 90 days, and optionally one campaign, one list or one member's campaigns. The choice is kept in the address, so a view can be shared as a link.
GuidedTours.dashboard_1_body: Each figure is set beside the period before. A reply is counted for the message it answers, so a week is not credited with answers to older mail.
GuidedTours.dashboard_2_body: Added up over the campaigns that are running. Switch it to LinkedIn or email alone with the button at its corner.
GuidedTours.dashboard_3_body: A mailbox that paused itself, an account that signed out, a limit about to be reached. Each has a button to the screen that deals with it, and goes away by itself once it is dealt with.
GuidedTours.dashboard_4_body: What has gone out today, set against what your senders are allowed to send.
GuidedTours.campaigns_0_body: With where each stands and what has come of it: who is enrolled, how many replied, how many accepted.
GuidedTours.campaigns_1_title: Start one, or take the list away
GuidedTours.campaigns_1_body: New campaign opens the setup: the list, the brief for the AI writer, the steps, the senders, and a check before launch.
GuidedTours.campaigns_2_body: Filter by status, channel or owner. Tick several to pause, resume, duplicate or archive them together. A draft opens its setup; anything else opens its own pages.
GuidedTours.campaign_0_body: Overview for results, Sequence for the steps, Prospects for the people in it, Settings for who it sends from and what it tracks.
GuidedTours.campaign_1_body: The rates and the chart are for what was sent in the period. The funnel and the A/B results are for the whole campaign.
GuidedTours.campaign_2_body: Share report makes a link for someone with no account. Add prospects enrols more contacts in a campaign that is already running.
GuidedTours.sequence_0_body: LinkedIn steps and email steps each run in their own order. A condition can hand a contact from one track to the other, or stop there.
GuidedTours.sequence_1_body: Edits are kept as a draft. Publishing puts them live; contacts part-way through stay on the step they were on.
GuidedTours.inbox_0_body: Email and LinkedIn conversations land here together. The number is the conversations waiting on you.
GuidedTours.inbox_1_body: Filters on the left, conversations in the middle, the thread on the right with what the reply seems to want and a suggested next step.
GuidedTours.contacts_0_body: With how interested they seem, who owns them, the lists and campaigns they are in, and when they last heard from you.
GuidedTours.contacts_1_body: Filter by campaign, intent, owner or tag and keep a filter as a saved view. Tick several to add them to a campaign, tag them or export them.
GuidedTours.lists_0_body: A campaign runs over a list. Fill one from a CSV file or a Sales Navigator search, or by hand.
GuidedTours.lists_1_body: Create a list, then import into it. Duplicates are matched before anything is added.
GuidedTours.companies_0_body: Every company you have a contact at, with how interested it seems, how many people you know there, and whether email to its domain is bouncing.
GuidedTours.companies_1_title: The list, and the company beside it
GuidedTours.companies_1_body: Pick a company to read what is known about it, the people you have there, people worth adding, and the signals about it. Mark it a target account to keep it in view.
GuidedTours.companies_2_body: Looking companies up on Apollo fills in funding, headcount and tools. It spends Apollo credits, so the cost is shown first and nothing is spent until you agree.
GuidedTours.pipeline_0_body: Opportunities by stage, with the tasks, meetings and activity that go with them. Each of those also has a view of its own, chosen beside the title.
GuidedTours.pipeline_1_title: Move a card as it progresses
GuidedTours.pipeline_1_body: Drag an opportunity to its next stage, or open it to change the amount, the owner or the close date. Won and lost are stages too.
GuidedTours.pipeline_2_body: Show everyone's or one member's. A positive reply can open an opportunity by itself; that is a setting under Edit stages.
GuidedTours.linkedin_0_body: Each has its own daily limits, working hours and weekly invitation limit, and warms up gradually when it is new.
GuidedTours.linkedin_1_body: Sign in through Linki or with a session cookie. Nothing runs on LinkedIn until an account is signed in.
GuidedTours.linkedin_2_body: Today's use against each limit. An account that reaches its weekly invitations waits by itself; the others carry on.
GuidedTours.mailboxes_0_body: Grouped by sending domain, with each domain's SPF, DKIM and DMARC at a glance.
GuidedTours.mailboxes_1_body: A daily limit that ramps up, warm-up, and a guard that pauses the mailbox if bounces or complaints climb. Open one to test it or change how it sends.
GuidedTours.deliverability_0_body: Per sending domain: its health, its DNS records with what to fix, what the guards have done, and who must not be contacted.
GuidedTours.deliverability_1_body: Run a placement test to see where mail from each mailbox lands, and re-check DNS after changing a record.
GuidedTours.ai_0_body: The model, a fallback for when it is unavailable, your tone and examples, and what each campaign's steps ask for.
GuidedTours.ai_1_body: Set a monthly budget. When it is reached, AI-written steps wait rather than fail, and you are told.
GuidedTours.templates_0_body: A library by channel and category. A step in a sequence can draw on one template, or rotate through several.
GuidedTours.templates_1_body: Each template shows how often it has been used and how many of those sends were answered.
GuidedTours.signals_0_body: A hire, a funding round, a change of tools: things that happened at an account you care about.
GuidedTours.signals_1_title: The feed, the rules, and detection
GuidedTours.signals_1_body: Rules decide what a signal does, such as enrolling the contact in a campaign. Detection looks for new ones on a schedule, within a monthly cap you set.
GuidedTours.csv_import_0_title: Four steps, and you can leave
GuidedTours.csv_import_0_body: Upload the file, match its columns to fields, decide what to do with people you already have, then check before anything is added. An import you leave can be picked up again.
GuidedTours.team_0_body: Invite people and give each a role, from viewer to owner. Every change is written to the audit log below.
GuidedTours.developers_0_body: API keys with their own rate limits, webhooks with a delivery log, and the address an AI client connects to over MCP.
